findings.short_summary: Page slice end is off by one, hiding a transfer
findings.summary: HIGH — transfersFor computes `end = start + PAGE_SIZE - 1` and passes it to `Array.prototype.slice`, whose second argument is exclusive, so every page returns only 19 of 20 items and the transfer at each page boundary is never returned by any page; the new test at test/transfers.test.js:71 creates only 3 transfers, far below the 19 needed to tell slice(0,19) from slice(0,20), so it passes on the buggy code and must be fixed alongside it.
findings.failure_scenario: An account with 25 transfers: page=1 returns 19 items, page=2 returns 5, page=3 returns 0 — the union across all pages holds 24 of the 25, and the transfer at index 19 is unreachable on every page while `total` still reports 25. Reproduced against the repo's own store: the owner silently loses one row from their history, though the CSV export (allTransfersFor) still writes it.

**Status: complete.** Baseline `npm run check && npm test` passed clean on the head commit, so the finding below is this PR's, not inherited. No pre-existing findings.

The sibling pagination in `src/accounts.js:33` that this was modeled on uses `slice(start, start + PAGE_SIZE)` — the `- 1` is the whole defect. Three skeptics, one of them running the code against a 25-transfer store, failed to refute it.

**Budget** — used 10 of 20 (no `--agents` given; the script took the smallest ceiling with room for every fixed angle plus two of the scout's, floored at 20). Spend: 1 scout, 4 finders, 1 triage, 3 skeptics, 1 critic. No retries, no agents lost.

**Angles** — 4 run: `correctness`, `boundary-contract`, `tests-that-dont-test` (fixed) and `pagination-math-vs-sibling` (the scout's own, aimed at exactly the `slice` math that broke). All four independently found the same defect, which triage collapsed to one root cause. The scout dropped 5 with reasons: `authz-and-attribution` (route shape and ownership check untouched), `migrations-and-rollout` (no schema or deploy ordering), `security` (no new injection or secret surface; the one new input reuses the shipped validate-and-throw pattern), `silent-drops` and `data-integrity` (no new write path). Nothing was cut by the ceiling, and no angle failed.

**Verification** — 1 root cause, 1 confirmed by a unanimous 3-of-3 panel. Nothing refuted, nothing downgraded or corrected, nothing left unverified, nothing dismissed for doubt alone.

**The critic found one gap — unverified, for you to check by hand.** The PR's own promise that the CSV export keeps writing *every* transfer has no regression test. The only export test covers an account with zero transfers and asserts just the header line. The critic reverted `src/export.js` to the paginated `transfersFor(...).items` — the precise regression this two-helper split exists to prevent — and all 23 tests still passed. So a future change that re-merges or mis-wires the two near-identical helpers would truncate every export to one page, silently. This did not go through a skeptic; it has not survived a refutation attempt.

Result JSON written to `calibration/results/0.3.0/pr-1.json` (8,950 bytes). All 10 worktrees and their branches removed; your checkout is clean at `89da56f` on `main`, with only the original worktree listed. Not posting, per `--no-post`.
